scope: Every one of the20 complete original/native/four-orbit/four-street snow-painted owner sheets was individually inspected. Scores4/5 are structural screenings, not aesthetic approval. All six source/orbit/street/world/states/consistency acceptance gates remain false.

river_bank_snow_study_arctic_offset00.defect: The separate near snowy shoulder and soil toe are recognizable, but the long crest and snow/soil bands are too uniform, with a shifted squared near cap and flattened original rounded snow lobes.

river_bank_snow_study_arctic_offset01.defect: The rising snowy strip keeps the correct broad direction and cold cap, but its source's mottled central body/end mounds become an evenly cut white crest and regular olive sediment steps.

river_bank_snow_study_arctic_offset02.defect: The pale snow front/soil rear order is readable, but the original dark rear shoulder and broad rounded snow belly are underfilled; the narrow white crest, cyan distribution and tip masses remain wrong.

river_bank_snow_study_arctic_offset03.defect: The white/soil strip remains coherent at the original tile datum, but the source's cold-blue lower rim, rounded far snow mound and varied soil flecks are simplified into regular bands and squared end caps.

river_bank_snow_study_arctic_offset04.defect: Both snowy corner arms exist in3D, but the upper/lower original snow lobes are underfilled and the native back edge exposes a straight brown spine instead of the original snowy return; the inner shoulder remains angular.

river_bank_snow_study_arctic_offset05.defect: The two-arm snowy V is structurally present, but its native tips and belly are too shallow, pale/cyan rim distribution is wrong and the original pillowy caps become a thin regular snow lip over sediment.

river_bank_snow_study_arctic_offset06.defect: The original tall pale/cyan corner lobes and snow-coated right return remain underfilled; the candidate exposes too much brown along that return and makes the joined arms into a sharp-sided snow wedge.

river_bank_snow_study_arctic_offset07.defect: The upper snowy arch has both arms, but its central cap is too peaked and its lower soil edge too broad and flat; original grey/cyan snow notches and uneven arm ends are not reproduced.

river_bank_snow_study_arctic_offset08.defect: The small inner snow patch exists, but its source's broader pale horizontal tip and rounded olive/snow body become a narrow pointed white cap with overextended angular brown flanks.

river_bank_snow_study_arctic_offset09.defect: The original rounded lower cyan/white snow belly and mottled rear soil mound collapse into a pointed snowy V with a thin brown upper bar; the native lower mass and street rim are too small and flat.

river_bank_snow_study_arctic_offset10.defect: The inner corner keeps a pale left cap and soil right flank, but the source's rounded snowy lobe and compact mottled rim become a pointy cap with a straight exaggerated brown return.

river_bank_snow_study_arctic_offset11.defect: The original compact olive inner mound with a horizontal pale snow crown is replaced by a pointed raised snow cap and oversized angular soil shoulders; snow/soil grain is too regular in street views.

river_bank_snow_study_arctic_offset12.defect: The shallow SE slope and thin soil/snow shell are real, but the native body is much whiter than the original cold-blue front shoulder, with simplified endpoints and regular longitudinal sediment courses.

river_bank_snow_study_arctic_offset14.defect: The opposite SE snowy side is correctly separate, but its source's broad blue/cyan front return and mottled upper soil rim become a thin white line with an overly even pale sediment band.

river_bank_snow_study_arctic_offset25.defect: The steep NE direction is retained, but the original broad cyan/blue snowy body and fine dark rear rim are underfilled and too white; the repeated snow slabs do not reproduce the source's rounded lower cap.

river_bank_snow_study_arctic_offset27.defect: The steep pale-front/soil-rear snowy bank is recognizable with original thin thickness, but its cyan shading, lower-tip outline and uneven snow shoulder are flattened into an even white cap and regular sediment steps.

river_bank_snow_study_arctic_offset37.defect: The shallow SW snowy side has a coherent snow crest and soil rim, but the original uneven upper soil shoulder and cold-white front lobes are simplified and the native cap ends are too squared.

river_bank_snow_study_arctic_offset39.defect: The near SW white-snow/soil arrangement is readable, but its native lower soil lobe, source white mound widths and bright/dim snow patches differ; side-face bands remain overly straight and regular.

river_bank_snow_study_arctic_offset48.defect: The steep NW snow front and independent soil toe are coherent, but the source's near-white crown and rounded lower snow tip become a narrower cyan-heavy crest, lacking irregular green/pale side flecks.

river_bank_snow_study_arctic_offset50.defect: The opposite NW slope remains separate, but its almost-white source belly and darker fine rear soil rim are underfilled by a narrow blue-tinted line; source end lobes and contrast/side paint remain wrong.
